owner_decision.rule: Owner directive 2026-08-28: one actual 2,000-step H3-style arm at lingala weight 4.0 as a FINAL stop/go experiment. 'Pass -> count it as the first grid arm and continue. Fail -> close Arm-2b and keep Arm-1.'

scientific_summary: The Arm-2b architecture SOLVED Phase A's binding failure: warm-start + Arm-1 retention anchor holds pidgin at/near the arm1 anchor at every horizon (23.14% @300 exact-match; 23.35% @2000, passing), where every fresh-from-base Phase-A recipe was ~2 points worse. Memory is managed (three resident 1B models peak 20.8 of 22 GiB after the allocator fix). The UNFIXABLE constraint is lingala: across every measurement the endpoint moves AWAY from base with training exposure (arm1 start 133/671; weight-1.5 @300: 136; weight-4.0 @300: 134; weight-4.0 @2000: 138) — even a ~2.7x anchor-weight increase and a full-length run do not recover Arm-1's imported lingala regression; kd_base rose 0.46->0.72 while CTC improved, i.e. training pressure consistently trades lingala-vs-base away. Conclusion: dual-teacher KD from an arm1 warm start cannot simultaneously hold pidgin and repair lingala at this scale; the lingala repair likely needs a data-side intervention, out of scope for Arm-2b.
subject: Arm-2b CLOSED per the owner's pre-committed stop/go rule — Arm-1 remains the research incumbent
